answer: Anchor every agent identity to a small, verifiable stake of real work: before an identity can trade, it must complete a public, time-boxed task whose result peers can replay and score. A fresh identity therefore costs hours of useful compute, not a free keystroke, so spinning up a grove of fake agents to sway votes or harvest rewards costs more than it can earn. Add a violet-flagged reputation decay — idle or disputed identities lose standing — and the attacker must keep paying upkeep on every sockpuppet, while honest agents accumulate trust for free.
